task.instruction:
Choose the rollout plan for a new support-triage model before a contractual launch date.

Recommend staged rollout or full rollout. State the first checkpoint and the observation that would change the recommendation.

evidence.content: A 20% staged rollout can run for five business days, has a ten-minute rollback, and will delay a common workflow by one week.
A full rollout meets the contractual date and removes 90 staff-hours of parallel queue management each week.
Offline tests show equal average accuracy, but only 120 escalated tickets represent the highest-risk queue.
Both options preserve customer-data controls and use the same audited model version.

target_a.content:
Situation: A payments team must replace a routing rule before a seasonal traffic peak.
Evidence:
[history-01-e1] A 10% canary would reveal error-rate changes within six hours and can be rolled back in four minutes.
[history-01-e2] A single cutover would eliminate 60 staff-hours of dual-route support, but rollback would take one day.
Decision: Run the 10% canary and expand only after the six-hour error review.
Reasoning: The canary buys decision-relevant evidence while preserving a fast exit.

Situation: A buyer must choose how to onboard a packaging supplier whose quality is promising but not yet proven at volume.
Message: We considered [history-02-e1] A 30-day order covers current demand and can be cancelled without penalty. [history-02-e2] An annual order is 18% cheaper and reserves the only production slot that supports the planned launch date. The decision is Place the 30-day order and inspect defect rates before reserving the annual slot.
Reasoning: The short order tests the uncertain quality claim without locking the launch into it.

Situation: Four support teams need one intake workflow, but the two proposed workflows have only small-sample evidence.
Record: [history-03-e1] A two-week trial can compare resolution time on 80 tickets without changing existing queues. [history-03-e2] Maintaining both workflows costs each team five hours per week and produces inconsistent customer handoffs.
Recorded decision: Trial both workflows for two weeks and choose using resolution and handoff results.
Reasoning: The available comparison can resolve the open question before the organization commits.

situation=A city must decide whether to expand a weekend permit service after a crowded one-day event. evidence=[history-04-e1] A four-week district pilot would measure repeat demand for $24,000 and can use existing staff. [history-04-e2] A citywide schedule would cost $110,000 but would give residents one consistent rule before the holiday season. decision=Run the district pilot and publish the demand threshold for citywide expansion.
Reasoning: One busy event is not enough to justify a permanent schedule when a bounded test is available.

Situation: An editorial team must book contributors for either a two-episode trial or an eight-part season.
Evidence:
[history-05-e1] The trial can be produced with current staff and would reveal completion and audience-retention rates.
[history-05-e2] The full season secures all contributors now, but cancellation would forfeit 35% of the production budget.
Decision: Produce the two-episode trial before exercising the season option.

Situation: An emergency hotfix could restore checkout quickly by sending unredacted payment logs to a shared channel.
Message: We considered [history-06-e1] The shared channel is accessible to contractors who are not authorized to view payment data. [history-06-e2] A redacted diagnostic takes 25 minutes longer and preserves the existing access controls. The decision is Reject the unredacted hotfix and use the redacted diagnostic path.

Situation: A school can run a fast scheduling experiment only by removing a student's required accessibility support for one week.
Record: [history-07-e1] The support is part of the student's approved accommodation plan. [history-07-e2] A slower scheduling test can preserve the support and still produce results within three weeks.
Recorded decision: Keep the required support and use the slower scheduling test.

situation=A routine dependency patch has passed the standard regression suite and does not change team workflows. evidence=[history-08-e1] The approved maintenance window includes an automated rollback. [history-08-e2] No customer data, staffing dependency, or unresolved performance question is involved. decision=Apply the patch through the approved maintenance path.
